subject: biology
title: Predator and Prey
welcome_lead: Watch the dance between hunters and the hunted, and how their numbers rise and fall.
meta_desc: KS3 Biology adventure on predator-prey relationships and population cycles.
final_note: You can now explain why predator and prey numbers rise and fall together.

concepts.def: Animal that hunts and eats prey.
Animal that is hunted for food.
Number of one species in a place.
Repeating pattern of rise and fall.
Living things and their environment together.

walkthroughs.body_html: A predator hunts; the prey is eaten. Foxes hunt rabbits; owls hunt mice. Predators usually have keen senses and speed.
When prey numbers rise, predators have more food and grow in number. More predators then reduce prey, so predator numbers fall. The cycle repeats.
Predators help control prey populations and keep ecosystems balanced. Remove a predator and prey can become too many, damaging the habitat.

numericals.q: There are 200 rabbits and predators eat 30 per month. How many left after 1 month?
